evaluator_limitations.finding: source_identity uses native str(relative_path), producing different digests from identical bytes on Windows versus POSIX; the portable wrapper repairs serialization only.

Checks source digest and record digest, but no explicit expected record set/count or protocol_sha256 check. An incomplete or empty glob can receive PASS. This audit independently verifies all expected file sets and all 360 record protocol digests.

Same incomplete/empty-glob weakness; runner_sha256 pins only run_repair.py, excluding imported features/digest/namespace implementations and explicit protocol identity. Package manifest supplies broader source integrity in this audit.

Posterior restore checks the mean/covariance implied by stored sufficient statistics; the verifier does not independently recompute those statistics from raw trace observations or replay acquisition decisions. Full new runs add evidence but use the same algorithm.

Source identity covers sklab/*.py plus run_study.py; it excludes verify_results.py, run_all.py, analyze_results.py, tests, and protocol files. Separate manifest/command/protocol hashes remain necessary.

Runner source identity hashes code/*.py recursively, but omits tests and protocols from the resume contract; test/analysis jobs record no output artifact hashes. Consequently the runner alone is not a complete frozen evaluator or protocol boundary.

Exact float-derived coefficient hashes and JSON sizes are platform-sensitive and checked before numerical comparisons; hash mismatch is a real strict replay failure, not numerical disproof of the mechanism result.

Fixed Gaussian representation and empirical sparse selection/qualification do not model structural uncertainty or learn applicability. Guard envelope is declared; extrapolation diagnostics intentionally score outside it.
